audit_findings.title: Wilson Wolf’s mandatory acquisition payment is omitted
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed payment approximately $1.0 billion plus unquantified contingent consideration; $6.03 per diluted share undiscounted and 23.3%-32.6% of stated scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: The mandatory cash outflow belongs in the equity bridge or acquisition-period cash flows, while Wilson Wolf’s post-acquisition owner earnings must enter OE concurrently.
audit_findings.evidence: The second option payment of approximately $1 billion plus potential contingent consideration is forecasted to occur between fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated omission of a contractually required payment, not merely a possible liability. Its gross size is capable of materially reducing standalone value, although the net direction cannot be determined because the acquired 80.1% earnings, contingent consideration, funding cost, timing, and merger consequences are unmodeled.
audit_findings.action: Rerun acquisition scenarios using the contractual payment date, contingent-payment formula, financing terms, and Wilson Wolf OE attributable to the acquired 80.1%; confirm whether the Merck merger modifies, assumes, or terminates the forward contract.

audit_findings.title: Wilson Wolf may be counted in both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed equity-method results were $(6.841) million in FY2024, $0.938 million in FY2025, and $0.887 million in FY2026; conditional capitalization of the FY2026 amount equals approximately $11.8 million or $0.07 per share, 0.32% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If FY2026 equity-method income remains in anchor OE while the $230.827 million Wilson Wolf carrying value is included in stakes_net, the same investment is represented in both operating value and the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company initially records its equity method investments at the amount of the Company’s investment and adjusts each period for the Company’s share of the investee’s income or loss and dividends paid.
audit_findings.explanation: The record does not demonstrate whether the OE calculation purged the income, so the possible classification error remains unresolved. Nevertheless, the filed FY2026 equity-method gain is only 0.37% of the $240.4 million anchor OE; even capitalized using the stated base operating-PV-to-anchor ratio, it changes base value by only about $0.07 per share and cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace each OE year to the filed equity-method gain or loss and distributions, document any exclusion, and correct the series if necessary; no broader input change is warranted from the supplied amounts.

audit_findings.title: The merger creates an unmodeled contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed Company termination fee $230.5 million ($1.39 per share; 6.2% of base equity value) and Parent reverse termination fee $576.1 million ($3.48 per share; 15.5% of base equity value); probability-weighted amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Scenario-specific termination payments would be added to or deducted from the equity bridge rather than historical OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company will be required to pay Parent a termination fee of approximately $230.5 million under specified circumstances, including termination of the Merger Agreement in connection with our entry into an agreement with respect to a Superior Proposal (as defined in the Merger Agreement) at any time prior to us receiving shareholder approval of the Merger Agreement, or termination by Parent if the Company’s Board of Directors effects a Change of Company Recommendation (as defined in the Merger Agreement).
audit_findings.explanation: The contractual claims and their gross amounts are demonstrated, but neither is unconditional. The Company fee reduces value in specified termination cases, while the larger Parent fee increases value only under specified regulatory-failure cases. Without scenario probabilities and confirmation that all contractual conditions are met, the record cannot establish their expected-value materiality.
audit_findings.action: Build mutually exclusive completion and termination scenarios from the merger agreement, assign supportable probabilities, verify each fee condition, and rerun the bridge using probability-weighted net proceeds or payments.

audit_findings.title: Dollar-for-dollar cash credit may ignore repatriation leakage
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed foreign-held cash proxy $124.912 million ($264.712 million total cash less $139.8 million held in the U.S.), equal to $0.75 per share and 3.4% of base equity value; actual leakage unquantified. The entire $265.479 million cash/STI bridge is $1.60 per share and 7.2% of base equity value.
audit_findings.mechanism: Taxes, restrictions, or required operating liquidity would reduce the cash and short-term-investment amount credited in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has not provided deferred taxes on approximately $ 131 million of undistributed earnings from non-U.S. subsidiaries as of June 30, 2026 which are indefinitely reinvested in operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and amount of any leakage are unresolved, and the $131 million of indefinitely reinvested earnings is not itself a cash balance. Even treating all computed foreign cash as unavailable would reduce base value by only about $0.75 per share; removing the entire cash/STI bridge would reduce it by about $1.60 per share, leaving every scenario far below the $72.43 market price. The issue therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied scale.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by jurisdiction, identify restricted and minimum operating cash, calculate applicable withholding and state taxes, and reduce the bridge only by evidenced unavailable amounts.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2023 residual $29.7 million, equal to 27.7% of filed D&A; residual amounts and eligibility for other years are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual depreciation or amortization proven to be an eligible non-economic charge would be added back to OE; a qualifying FY2026 amount could raise the latest-year anchor and operating DCF.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2023 $29.7m (27.7% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: Leaving unidentified D&A as an expense is a demonstrated conservative treatment, but it is not a demonstrated valuation error because eligibility has not been established. Adding the supplied FY2023 amount alone would not change the $240.4 million latest-actual anchor because the stated trend already exceeds it. Materiality remains unresolved because no FY2026 residual or classification evidence was supplied.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile filed D&A by asset class for every OE year, determine which residual components are eligible add-backs, and rerun only if filed evidence establishes an eligible amount in FY2026 or otherwise changes the MIN(trend, latest) anchor.
